title: Analysis of microplastics in the environment using pyrolysis-GC/MS
author: Santos, Insa, et al.
materials: Overall, the described Pyr-GC/MS methodology showed a good performance for the simultaneous identification and quantification of 12 of the most common plastic polymers in microplastics samples. Furthermore, the use of the commercial software F-Search and F-Search MPs, which include pyrolyzates and polymers libraries, allowed the establishment of simple and useful analytical workflows that enabled a fast identification and quantification of plastic polymers in environmental samples.

steps.title: Configure Pyr‑GC/MS instrument parameters
steps.instruction: Set the pyrolysis furnace to 600 °C and hold for 0.2 min; set the pyrolysis transfer line to 300 °C. Configure the GC injector in split mode with a 50:1 split ratio at 300 °C. Install the Ultra Alloy UA+-5 capillary column (5% diphenyl‑95% dimethylpolysiloxane, 30 m × 0.25 mm i.d., 0.25 µm film) together with a 1 m × 0.1 mm deactivated fused‑silica post‑column. Use helium (purity 6.0) as carrier gas at a flow rate of 1.37 mL/min. Program the GC oven: 2 min at 40 °C, then increase 20 °C/min to 320 °C and hold for 16 min. Set the detector transfer line to 320 °C. Operate the mass spectrometer with electron‑ionization at 70 eV, quadrupole temperature 150 °C, source temperature 230 °C, acquiring full‑scan spectra from m/z 29 to 400 at 2 scan/s.

steps.title: Prepare calibration standards in cups
steps.instruction: Using an XP6 microbalance (readability 1 µg, six‑decimal display), weigh 0.4 mg, 1.0 mg, 2.0 mg and 4.0 mg of the commercial mixture of the 12 most common polymers (polystyrene, polyethylene, polypropylene, polyvinylchloride, polyethylene terephthalate, polycarbonate, polyurethane, Nylon 6, Nylon 66, polymethyl methacrylate, styrene‑butadiene copolymer, acrylonitrile‑butadiene‑styrene) that contains CaCO₃ as inert diluent, into separate pyrolysis cups. Add quartz wool equal to 20 % of the weighed amount, placed with tweezers so the sample is completely covered.

steps.title: Prepare environmental samples in cups
steps.instruction: Weigh 0.25 mg of each collected microplastic sample into a pyrolysis cup, cover with quartz wool (amount equal to 20 % of the sample weight) using tweezers, and prepare each sample in triplicate.

steps.title: Run Pyr‑GC/MS analysis
steps.instruction: Place each prepared cup into the Auto‑Shot sampler and perform a single‑shot pyrolysis at 600 °C (0.2 min hold) with online transfer to the GC/MS under the instrument settings defined in Step 1. Acquire chromatograms and mass spectra for all calibration standards and environmental samples.

steps.title: Process data and record concentrations
steps.instruction: Use the F‑Search and F‑Search MPs software to identify polymer peaks, generate calibration curves from the four standard amounts, and quantify polymer amounts in each environmental sample. Record the mean concentrations (µg polymer per mg sample) as follows: S1 (Almadrava) PS 219.6 ± 15.2; S2 (Cala Montgó) PS 5.02 ± 3.10, PE 369.6 ± 12.2; S3 (Cala Montgó) PS 30.0 ± 32.0, PE 249.8 ± 9.7; S4 (Cala Montgó) PE 70.1 ± 15.6; S5 (Riuet) PS 331.5 ± 33.2; S6 (Riuet) PS 41.4 ± 40.7, PP 89.2 ± 15.6.
